life_history: The patient is a university student presenting with low self-efficacy and low problem recognition regarding her alcohol use. The target behavior, heavy and frequent drinking, has escalated over the years and is heavily utilized to manage academic stress, particularly upcoming midterms. The immediate precipitant leading to counseling is a recent alcohol-related injury: she sprained her ankle after impulsively jumping off a bus in stilettos during a weekend pub crawl, and she attends the current session hungover, initially minimizing her drinking as typical student behavior.
intermediate_beliefs: Positive assumption: If I engage in heavy drinking, then I can cope with academic stress and fit in with my peers; negative assumption: If I stop drinking, then the distress of university midterms will overwhelm me and I will fall behind or be socially isolated.
intermediate_beliefs_during_depression: If I try to reduce my drinking to the safe guidelines and fail because of my high tolerance, it proves I have no willpower and cannot handle the pressures of university life.
coping_strategies: Maladaptive compensatory coping includes binge drinking (up to 7-8 drinks) on weekends to socialize, drinking daily (1-2 beers) to manage academic stress, and defensive minimization (insisting her use is normal for students). Adaptive/harm-reduction coping includes recognizing that hangovers severely impair her productivity, admitting her rising tolerance is concerning, and agreeing to attend a follow-up counseling session when sober.

cognitive_models.situation: Coming home from the university library after a long, exhausting day of studying for upcoming midterms.
cognitive_models.automatic_thoughts: I need a beer or two to relax. It is completely normal for university students to drink to cope with this kind of stress.
cognitive_models.behavior: Drinking 1 to 2 beers alone at home to decompress from academic pressure.

cognitive_models.situation: Attending a 90s-themed pub crawl on the weekend, having already consumed several drinks, and seeing her friends walking ahead of her.
cognitive_models.automatic_thoughts: I need to catch up with my friends. It is a really good idea to just jump off the stairs of the bus, even though I am wearing stilettos.
cognitive_models.behavior: Acting impulsively by jumping off the bus, resulting in a sprained ankle and intense embarrassment, alongside binge drinking 7 to 8 drinks.

cognitive_models.situation: Sitting in the counseling session, severely hungover, and hearing the counselor state that the low-risk limit is 10 drinks per week.
cognitive_models.automatic_thoughts: Wow, I drink a little over that, especially with midterms. I have built up my tolerance over the years. This is a little bit concerning. I definitely do not feel good right now.
cognitive_models.behavior: Initially acting defensive, then admitting concern about her tolerance, acknowledging the health and productivity benefits of cutting back, and agreeing to schedule another appointment.
